Indian benchmark indices ended lower on Monday after the Closing Auction Session, with the Sensex falling over 300 points and the Nifty settling at 24,080.40.
At close, the Sensex was down 307.68 points, or 0.40 percent, at 76,956.83, while the Nifty fell 95.25 points, or 0.39 percent.

Media and metal stocks led the sectoral losses, falling more than 2 percent each, while FMCG declined 1.69 percent. Banking and pharma stocks bucked the weakness, with private banks gaining nearly 1 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Down)
GIFT Nifty was trading marginally lower at around 24,206.50 in early trade, indicating a flat to negative opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Mixed)
Asian markets were trading mixed in the early trade on Tuesday.
US Equities (Slip)

U.S. stocks weakened on Monday, with Wall Street turning the page on a volatile ​month as a war-related jump in crude prices revived inflation fears and raised the likelihood of tighter monetary policy.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 374.09 points, or 0.70%, to 53,185.90, the S&P 500 lost 25.62 points, or 0.33%, to 7,686.14 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 31.53 points, or 0.12%, to 26,370.89.
Dollar Index (Down)
The dollar index was down marginally against other major currencies.
US Bond Yield (Up)

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose two basis points to 4.77%, its highest level since January 2025. The yield on the 10-year Japanese government bond rose to 2.965% after touching a three-decade high in the previous session.
Asian currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar, with the Malaysian ringgit and Indonesian rupiah among the notable decliners, while the Taiwan dollar and Chinese renminbi gained. The Malaysian ringgit fell 0.218%, followed by the Indonesian rupiah, down 0.164%, and the South Korean won, which slipped 0.177%. The Singapore dollar declined 0.047%, while the Thai baht and Japanese yen eased 0.039% and 0.019%, respectively. On the positive side, the Taiwan dollar rose 0.19%, the Chinese renminbi gained 0.146%, and the Philippine peso strengthened 0.136%.
Crude (Gains)
Oil rose for a second session as fresh hostilities between the US and Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent traded around $91 a barrel after US forces hit an island in Hormuz, and Iran retaliated with attacks on the United Arab Emirates and Jordan, marking the first exchange of fire in about a month. West Texas Intermediate was above $86 after advancing 2.8% on Monday, the biggest gain in three weeks.
Gold (Up)

Gold steadied after a two-day drop as the US and Iran exchanged strikes for the first time in a month, raising the odds of rising energy costs pushing up inflation and pressuring the Federal Reserve to lift interest rates.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) intensified their selling on August 31, offloading nearly Rs 8,000 crore worth of equities. In contrast, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to support the market, buying equities worth Rs 4,588 crore during the session.
